watches.name: Gates of the Arctic Caribou
watches.description: The Gates of the Arctic watch displays daytime from 6 am to 6 pm with a north star pointing to the hours and a moon for the hours between 6 pm and 6 am representing the limited amounts of daylight during winter in Alaska. Each hour is denoted by a white star/dot in the night sky. The minutes are shown inside the mountain peak. And when the lights go out, the luminescent northern lights begin to glow. Illustrated by Kenneth Crane.

watches.name: Space Shuttle Jump Hour Automatic
watches.description: Honoring NASA’s space shuttle program, which carried hundreds of astronauts on important missions for three decades, this jump hour automatic watch shows the hours in the moon and the minutes are revealed in the clouds. What is a jump hour? A jump hour watch is a unique timepiece where the hour indicator does not slowly sweep across the dial. Instead, it displays the hour numerically in a small window and instantly "jumps" to the next number at the exact moment the 60th minute of the previous hour ends. Commissioned art was illustrated by Peter Greenwood. IG @petergreenwood_uk

watches.name: Happiness is Fleeting Jump Hour Automatic
watches.description: Illustrated by Kerry Callen, this poor zombie has lost his balloon -- and his arm. A playful way to display the time, the balloon is the minute hand and the hour can be seen in the cloud. Built on a Jump Hour automatic movement that can be manually wound via the crown or the rotor which can be seen through the exhibition caseback. No batteries. No charging. Automatic movements generate and store power from the motion of your wrist as you wear the watch. This collaboration is limited to just 999 pieces.
